  once, a screen window surviving the host's restart (the offline
  banner with the mode row disabled, then the pane refilled live once
  the watch was resent after `hello`), and a screen window reopened
  with its mode and content after the app was terminated. On the
  headset the first run showed a gap the simulator could not: a run
  that ends with only card windows is restored without the browser,
  and nothing started the connections either, since the boot lived in
  the main window's view. Every scene now boots the model (the first
  call does the work), the first card window to find the main window
  missing after the restoration grace opens it, and the card header
  carries a Sessions button that brings the main window forward (it
  is a value-keyed window group, so this never makes a second one).
  From the first hours with it: the card header is small (a short
  host pill, the Sessions button an icon) so a tall narrow card, the
  shape the conversation and document modes will want, holds
  together, and the mode pills are mini and become icons when the
  titles would wrap; the text of every mode but the card (the screen,
  the run output, the last response and the conversation, through an
  environment value the prose views size their fonts from) scales
  through a readout at the end of the mode row that opens a slider
  and snap sizes (50 to 200 percent), kept per window while it is open
  and starting over in
  a new one, since the comfortable size depends on where the window
  sits in the room. A pinch on the pane was tried first and did
  nothing on the headset, and a slider along the window's bottom edge
  was hard to take hold of next to the system's own bar, so the
  control moved up; the pinch may come back later.
  Milestone B runs on the headset, installed from the terminal with
  `client/scripts/device.sh` once the one-time Xcode setup was done
  (Developer Mode, the device paired in Xcode's Devices window, one
  run from Xcode with a development team on the target). Not in B: the
  conversation, last-response and run-output modes (Milestone C), the
  QR scanner (the invite is pasted or passed at launch), and the
  Xcode project is generated, not checked in.
- **C1 and C2, content on the wire and the conversation.** The port
  serves `session.conversation` (a page of turns from a number,
  stopping at `limit`, 100 at most, or the page's byte cap, with
  `next`; or anchored at its end with `from=last` or `before=n`,
  filling backward so the anchor is always in it, since a page of
  large turns walked forward from a count stopped short of the end and
  showed a stale tail; a page carries the first 512 bytes of each
  tool call's input and result, marked `more`, and
  `session.turn` reads one turn whole for a client that opened its
  activity, which cut a page of this project's own transcript from
  half a megabyte for six turns to a page of twenty; a client follows
  a change page after page to the end; a turn over 256 KiB loses its tool detail and
  notes first, then its prompt is shortened, then its answer is cut
  from the front, and says `truncated`), `session.last_response` (the
  last turn's answer, a projection of the conversation key at its
  revision), `session.runs` (from the record, artifacts by name) and
  `session.run_output` (the log's tail, 500 lines at most). The
  content worker reads them all: a transcript is parsed through the
  reader's new `read_masked`, which runs the mask over every text
  before the parser's caps, and the parsed, masked conversation stays
  on the worker by handle, file version and policy, so a poll is a
  stat and a page is served from memory; a run's log is read through
  `scrollback::tail_masked`, which starts the longest secret's length
  before the tail window so a value on the window's edge is masked
  whole, and is versioned by inode, change time and size. The key for
  a run is `record/n`, and the diff pass fingerprints a record's runs
  as the `runs` collection. Only a Claude Code session has a
  conversation; the rest are refused `no_conversation`. The client
  holds a conversation as pages merged by turn number (`ConversationState`):
  a `changed {conversation}` refetches from the last turn held, which
  replaces that turn and everything after, a page reaching the end
  drops anything after it, and another `resume_id` drops it all; the
  card windows draw Last response (the answer with its inline
  Markdown), Conversation (each turn's prompt, its activity folded
  under a line with the tool calls' input and result one level deeper,
  its answer; "Earlier turns" loads the page ending before the first held;
  the end follows the host) and Run output (a run picker with its
  status and the tail, scaled like the screen). Seen on the simulator
  against a throwaway host: a real transcript's last page scrolled to
  its end, and a service's run with its exit code and log. Not yet in
  C: `file.read` (no view asks for a file before Milestone D) and the
  policy reads off the frame.
- **C3, the control scope.** `POST sessions/{id}/send|resume|trust`
  for a device whose scope is `control` (a read device is refused
  `scope`, by name, with nothing run). The body carries the device's
  own operation id, `op`, and for a send the text (16 KiB at most).
  The request becomes the wire request the control socket would carry
  and goes through the same `serve`, so nothing new runs or logs: a
  send or a resume is written to `operations.log` before it runs, a
  repeat of the op is answered from the log without typing or
  launching again, and an op that was started and never answered is
  refused `interrupted` (409) rather than run twice. `/info` lists
  `control` among the capabilities and the send and op caps among the
  limits. The client makes a UUID per command and follows the spec's
  rule on a timeout: a status query, never a blind resend; `done`
  takes the logged reply (its failure reason included), `interrupted`
  is shown as started with the outcome unknown, `unknown` resends once
  with the same op. A `scope` refusal names the reason and keeps the
  pairing (only an unauthorized or revoked token drops it), and a
  timeout on a command does not count against the connection. The
  card window of a Claude session ends in a control bar: a message
  field with a microphone button that starts dictation at once
  through the Speech framework, on-device where the device has it,
  the words revised in place after what was typed (the keyboard's own
  mic still works; "look to dictate" is a system affordance of search
  fields only, and an app gets no gaze event, so the button is a tap),
  Send, "Trust this folder" when the session view
  carries the question, and Resume for a not-running session with a
  handle, behind "Resume spends a turn". The bar is disabled unless
  the session is live, and a read device sees why instead of the
  controls. Tests cover a read device refused, a send typed once for
  one op, a resume launching once, a running one launching nothing,
  trust answering the question once, the bad bodies, and the scope
  lowered again; on the client the op per command, the three status
  outcomes after a timeout, the one resend and the give-up, and the
  refusals.
- **C3, the draft.** An agent session's prompt as a device reads and
  works on it is its Prompt Box editor on the host, made on demand as
  the card's microphone makes one (`prompt_box::ensure_editor`).
  `GET sessions/{id}/draft` answers the editor's rendered text, the
  live utterance's range, its status and what undo, redo and the AI
  pass can do (`DraftView`); `POST` with `action` applies replace,
  undo, redo, clear, clean_up, delete_sentence or delete_paragraph,
  or `send` with the device's `op`, which takes the draft to the pane
  through `serve` as the plain send does and clears the editor (a
  repeat of a send that went is answered from the log; an empty draft
  is refused); `POST sessions/{id}/dictation` feeds a device's speech
  events (`started`, `voice_started`, `partial`, `final`,
  `voice_ended`, `stopped`, with the device's own recognizer session
  number) to the editor as `SpeechEventReceived`, so the device
  recognizes and the editor keeps the document. The drafts are
  fingerprinted every 150 ms while a subscriber is connected and an
  editor that moved emits `changed {draft, id}`; the device holding it
  re-reads. `/info` lists the `draft` capability. The client's
  control bar on such a host is a view of the editor: typing replaces
  the text once it pauses, dictation goes as speech events in order
  with a recognizer session per run, the tools sit above the field,
  Send goes through the draft under an op, and `changed {draft}`
  re-reads what a bar holds. The prompt window on the headset
  (`PromptWindowView`, one per app) shows the whole draft of the
  session whose input is active, the live utterance in amber, with a
  microphone, the tools and Send, the desktop preview's role for the
  Working Set. Known gaps: the AI
  pass runs in the editor's worker, pumped by the host's frame, so a
  host whose window is occluded finishes it on its next frame; the
  Mac's own voice runtime and a device dictate into the same editor
  under different session numbers, and nothing stops both at once.
- **C3, restoration.** A card window keeps its place in a
  conversation (`ConversationPlace`): the turn at the top of the view,
  or the end it follows, and the folds open per turn and per activity,
  keyed by the transcript's `resume_id`. The scroll view is positioned
  by turn number, so a page merging under the view keeps the turn at
  the top where it is, and "Earlier turns" pins the turn that was
  first; the end is followed only while the end marker is on screen,
  so reading an old turn while the agent works no longer jumps. The
  folds live in the window rather than the rows, so a turn replaced by
  a refetch, or the whole conversation dropped and re-read on a
  reconnect, comes back with the same folds open. The place is saved
  beside the window's mode in `presentation.json` (an older file reads
  with no place), so a relaunch restores it; a turn no longer held
  after a reconnect, or another transcript, falls back to the end.
- **C4, the policy off the frame and `file.read`.** The frame no
  longer resolves a redaction policy: a content job carries a
  `PolicySpec` (the project's environment, the sets it and the session
  may use, and `policy_epoch`, moved by every save and secret change)
  and the content worker reads the dotenv files and the secret store,
  caching the policy per spec for a minute, so a slow Keychain call
  costs the worker, never a frame; `Services.secrets` is an `Arc` for
  that. A store that fails refuses with `policy` (503) rather than
  answering unmasked. `GET projects/{id}/files/{path}` reads a file
  some working set pins (`PinTarget::File`), through
  `adapters::files::open_pinned`: the path checked before the disk,
  the root opened as a directory descriptor and every component
  opened from the previous one with `NOFOLLOW` (no symlink is followed,
  parent or leaf; macOS says `ENOTDIR` where Linux says `ELOOP`), the
  leaf non-blocking so a FIFO does not park the thread and checked to
  be a regular file, dotenv names refused whatever is pinned, the read
  one byte past the 768 KiB limit so growth cannot pass it, the version
  the inode, change time and size. The worker caches the masked file
  per key and re-reads only when the version or the policy moved; a
  watched file emits `changed {file, project/path}` on the poll.
  Refusals: `not_pinned` (404), `too_large` (413, with the size),
  `failed` (400) for a dotenv file, a symlink, a FIFO or a non-text
  file. The client holds files as content (`FileBody`, `watch(file:)`,
  re-read on `changed`); no window shows one yet, which the working set
  view brings. Milestone C is complete.
- **Scope on the listings.** A listing over the remote port leaves
  out the records Dispatch made for its own use (a ticket's project
  and its sessions, a worker session anywhere), told by the
  `<ticket>-<nonce>` op they were made under
  (`switchboard_control::is_dispatch_worker_op`); a supervisor's
  (`sup-…`) and the owner's own stay. `?scope=all` on `projects`,
  `sessions`, `waiting` and the `events` subscription lists and
  announces them, and a worker record is still read by its id, for
  the ticket view to come. Frames for a worker record go to `scope=all`
  subscribers alone. The control socket is untouched, so Dispatch sees
  everything as before.
- **On the headset (2026-10-14).** Scene restoration is ruled out: a
  launch opens the Sessions window and nothing else (the card and
  prompt window groups have `restorationBehavior(.disabled)`), after a
  restored window kept the process alive out of view so that an icon
  tap presented nothing. A launch log in the app's container
  (`launch.log`: launches, window appearances, scene phases) stands in
  for a device syslog the Mac cannot read. The conversation's end
  marker lives outside the lazy stack, so the follow button and
  opening at the end hold on the device. Following the end was then
  made a mode (2026-10-16): the view is held at the end with scrolling
  off, and anything growing under it pulls the end back on screen; a
  button at the right edge releases it to read, the ellipsis at the
  foot returns it. Before, following meant "the marker is on screen",
  and a new turn's row growing after the scroll landed pushed the
  marker off and turned following off by itself; the turn at the top
  was also a position bound to the scroll view, which re-applied it as
  the content grew and sent the view up. Markdown tables in an answer
  are laid out as grids. A Bonjour resolve that gets no answer is
  given up after 5 s, and each offline host resolves on its own task,
  after the retry loop hung on one resolve left waiting by the system.
- **Tickets on the headset (2026-10-17).** The port serves Dispatch's
  tickets from the app's own status poll (`src/core/tickets.rs`, spec
  §4.7): a listing by project with each ticket's standing worded as the
  Mac's page words it and its decisions; one ticket with its body,
  attempts and lanes; `decide` and `resume` under `control`, answered
  when Dispatch answers the call the Mac's action became
  (`TicketReply`, the content worker's deferred channel reused). The
  tickets are one fingerprinted collection, so a device hears one
  `changed tickets` frame per status that moved. The client lists them
  on a Tickets tab, oldest first within a project, urgent ones marked,
  with a detail view that answers decisions (the recommended option
  first, a note field, several options for a `multiple` one), resumes
  a parked ticket, and opens the project's supervisor session.
  The next day (2026-10-18) the attempts' files came: each attempt
  lists its artifacts, checks log, review rounds' files and evidence
  by a key that stands for the path, the port reads one as text
  through the Mac's own artifact read (from its cache while the ticket
  stands) or as an image from the disk, serves the ticket's events
  from the Mac's cache, and takes `close`; `info` lists `evidence` for
  it. The client's list is ordered last-moved-first with a menu for
  the order (waiting first, newest, by project), the hosts, projects
  and states (closed hidden unless asked), and a "waiting on me"
  switch; the detail shows each attempt's checks and rounds with a
  button per readable file, a Notes shortcut to the newest notes, a
  timeline, and Close. Left out for now: take, the console, the plan
  review's feedback flow; a worker session is named but not opened,
  since the plain listing hides worker records.
- **A session opened from the headset (2026-10-19).** The port takes
  `POST projects/{id}/sessions` under `control` (spec §4.5): the
  body's `op` the key, through the control socket's `session.new`,
  a Claude Code, Codex or shell session named by the device, in the
  project's root or a directory under it (`project_dir` in `app.rs`
  refuses a path that steps out or is not a directory), an agent's
  `prompt` its first turn on the command line. `info` lists `create`,
  and `/ops/{op}` names what a done creation made, so a lost reply
  still finds its record. The client offers a plus button on the
  Sessions tab and "New session in this project" on a listed session
  for a host that is connected, paired under `control` and serves
  `create`; the sheet (`NewSessionView.swift`) picks the host, the
  project by workspace, the kind, a name (defaulting to the kind's
  word and a count), a directory and the first message, and Start
  opens the session's window on the reply. Not from a device yet:
  commands and services, environment sets on the new session, a new
  project or workspace.
- **Pairing by the typed code (2026-10-14).** visionOS gives an app
  no camera, so the QR code is never scanned on the headset. A
  discovered host that is not paired offers Pair on the Servers screen:
  the client resolves its record, reads `/info` under no trust and
  shows the key the host presented in the dialog's own short form
  (`KeyFingerprint.short`, the first sixteen hex digits in fours), the
  owner compares it with the Key line on the Mac and types the
  eight-character code, and the pairing goes out pinned to that key
  (`ConnectionManager.lookup` and `pair(_:code:)`; the resolver is
  injectable for the tests). Pasting the invite's text stays as the
  fallback.
- **The web page (2026-10-22).** The remote port serves a browser page
  (`web/index.html`, `app.css`, `app.js`, embedded by `src/web.rs`) at
  `GET /`, `/app.css` and `/app.js`, before pairing, under a strict
  CSP. The pairing QR and "Copy invite" now carry one URL,
  `https://<ip>:<port>/#code=…&key=…&id=…` (`core::remote::pairing_invite`),
  so a phone's camera opens the page; the code rides in the fragment,
  which no request log can hold, and the page clears it before any
  request. The page pairs with `transport: "cookie"`, and the host sets
  the token as `switchboard_token_<server_id>` (`Secure; HttpOnly;
  SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v1/`), which `authenticate` reads when no
  bearer is sent and which a revoked token's 401 clears. The page lists
  sessions by project with the waiting ones first, shows a Claude Code
  session's last response or any other session's screen, and sends a
  reply under `control` scope; it polls over `fetch` and upgrades to
  the WebSocket when the browser allows one. The browser's trust step
  is the certificate warning (see `docs/remote-client.md` §5); the
  native clients still parse the earlier JSON invite. Not verified on
  a phone from here: whether a browser stores the `Secure` cookie from
  a bypassed-certificate origin, and whether iOS Safari carries the
  bypass to `wss://`.
- **Known gaps at the first merge.** Milestone D, the iPad shell, is
  not started. The Codex transcript parser, so a Codex session's
  conversation is empty on a device. The Dispatch ticket view
  (`scope=all` is served; no view asks for it). Removing dead sessions
  from a device. The Recent sessions set counts worker sessions. The
  screen and run-output modes follow the end without the
  conversation's end marker. The draft path makes the editor on the
  frame (`prompt_box::ensure_editor` reads the voice key there), so an
  unsigned host freezes on the Keychain prompt while a device asks for
  a draft; the signed bundle never prompts. Remote access off the LAN
  is §9 of the spec, deferred.

## Versioning and updates (2026-10-15)

The version in `Cargo.toml` is the one source, by semantic versioning,
and reaches the binary, the bundle's `Info.plist` and the host's
`/info` reply; `CHANGELOG.md` lists every user-visible change under
Unreleased until `scripts/bump.sh` dates it under the next version, and
`scripts/release.sh` publishes that version as a GitHub release tagged
`v<version>` with the signed bundle, its SHA-256 and the changelog
section as notes. The app updates itself from there: `core::updates`
checks twenty seconds after launch and hourly through the
`UpdateSource` port (`adapters::updates::GitHubReleases`, the fake in
tests), offers a newer release as a notice and a rail item, downloads
it on a click to a staging directory, checks the zip against its
published SHA-256 and the bundle with `codesign` against the running
app's Team ID, and on "Restart to update" arranges a helper that swaps
the bundle after the process exits, keeps the old one aside for a
failed copy, and relaunches. A pre-release or unparsable tag is never
offered; a bare binary or an unsigned bundle refuses to install.

## Token and time accounting (2026-10-20)

`dispatch report` and the ticket page's Usage tab show every session a
ticket started with its tokens by model (input, output, cache write
with its hour-long part, cache read) and its time: span, active (inside
turns), asking (an `AskUserQuestion` waiting on its answer) and idle
(between turns). The counts roll up per attempt, per stage and per
ticket, and across tickets in `report --project`. They are read from
Claude Code's transcripts after the fact; only counts, model names and
timestamps are kept, never message content.

The record keeps what the transcripts cannot be found again without.
`Ticket.transcripts` lists, per Switchboard record id, every
`TranscriptRef` (kind, provider id, path, when first seen), a `/clear`
adding one rather than replacing the last. `Attempt.run_sessions` keeps
a plan review's reviewer and planner, which only the workflow run names,
and `Attempt.agent` the kind of operator an agent attempt launched.
`SessionView.transcript` carries the path from the resume handle. The
runner notes a ref whenever it reads a session: the stage agent's poll
(`watched_view`), every review, fixer and rewriter poll (`seen`), the
first read of a run's sessions in `poll_workflow`, and
`retire_processes`, which notes a session before judging whether it
still runs, so one that exited long ago is still recorded at park and
close. `report --refresh` asks Switchboard once for a ticket from before
these fields and adds what it finds under the lock.

Each session counts within a window: from its attempt's start (its
round's, for a round's sessions) to where the next naming of the same
record id starts. The start drops a clone's copied history, whose
timestamps come before its attempt, and splits one session that two
attempts name. A plan review attempt's own `session` is the card's face
and is left to `run_sessions`. A message is written once per content
block with the usage growing, so the last record per `message.id` is
the message; `<synthetic>` is skipped; Agent-tool subagents' files under
`<transcript minus .jsonl>/subagents/` fold into their parent's tokens,
not its time. A session's kind is the one recorded beside its id, else
any ref's, else its operator in the ticket's pipeline copy, marked as
such. Codex and command sessions are not counted and show their round's
or attempt's span; a Claude session with no transcript read is "not
found", and one whose kind nothing says is "kind unknown", never zero.

The rows are cached in `<data>/tickets/<id>/usage.json`
(`store::USAGE_VERSION`, refused when newer), one entry per file with
its size, mtime and `read_ms`, so the counts outlive Claude Code's
deletion of transcripts after `cleanupPeriodDays`; a vanished file's
entry is kept and marked `gone`. A changed file is read again. Files
are read with the writer lock not held, and the lock is taken only to
merge by `read_ms` and write, so two writers keep each other's newer
entries. The close reads the counts once its processes are retired,
letting the runner's held lock go around the read as the tree removal
does. The port answers `usage` from the cache brought up to date, never
asking Switchboard.

Known gaps: a permission prompt's wait counts as active. A running
agent's counts on the tab are as of the ticket's last change. Codex is
not counted. A cold Usage read of a large open ticket holds the port's
handler for its duration. A ticket from before this change takes a
session's kind from its pipeline copy, which a restart may have
replaced. There are no prices: `Policy.rates` cannot price cache
writes and reads, and the cache keeps the hour-long split and `speed`
for a price table later. The session page counts each `message.id`
once and skips `<synthetic>`, as the tab does, but it reads only the
main transcript and counts an assistant record with no `message.id`
once, which the tab drops. The two agree only for a session with no
subagent files whose records all carry an id; a session whose
Agent-tool subagents wrote their own files shows fewer tokens on the
session page.

## Open questions

- Shared project config runs with a hash-and-approve flow and no
  sandbox. Should approved commands be restricted to the variables they
  list instead of receiving the whole project environment?
- Notes editor in scope, or "open in editor"? Leaning open in editor.
- Multiple machines: sync the project list early? Leaning no.

# Switchboard

A desktop app for organizing, managing, and automating agent coding
sessions. Built in Rust with [egui](https://docs.rs/egui) /
[eframe](https://docs.rs/eframe) from
[egui-app-template](../egui-app-template); design notes live in `docs/`.

Requires Rust 1.95 or newer.

## Development

```sh
cargo run --locked                                   # launch the app
cargo test --locked --workspace                      # unit + headless UI + tmux integration tests, every crate
cargo test --locked -p egui_term --lib               # the vendored terminal widget (outside the workspace)
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   # lint
cargo fmt --all                                      # format
(cd client && swift test)                            # the Swift client's packages, 81 tests (Xcode; not in the hook or CI)
(cd client && scripts/sim.sh run)                    # the visionOS app on the simulator (xcodegen; see client/README.md)
./scripts/test-times.sh                              # every test timed serially, the slowest ten, the budget checked
```

Test times. The budget is no test over 5 s and the whole workspace
under two minutes locally; `scripts/test-times.sh` checks the first and
exits non-zero past it. Measured on an M-series Mac with the script
(serial):

```
slowest ten:
  2.26 s  gate  project_config_is_listed_but_never_run_until_approved
  2.19 s  gate  killing_the_attached_client_keeps_the_session
  1.52 s  switchboard (lib)  ui::session::tests::a_dropped_terminal_releases_its_descriptors
  1.51 s  dispatch/dispatch (lib)  health::tests::a_socket_that_never_answers_times_out_and_one_that_does_is_timed
  0.88 s  dispatch/first_slice  a_lost_unmark_is_sent_again_until_it_lands
  0.74 s  dispatch/first_slice  keep_or_no_key_leaves_history_alone
  0.70 s  dispatch/first_slice  a_rebase_that_changes_nothing_or_past_the_cap_is_a_question
  0.66 s  gate  restart_reattaches_to_live_sessions
  0.62 s  dispatch/first_slice  a_branch_pushed_by_an_agent_is_not_rewritten_after_a_send_back
  0.60 s  switchboard (lib)  adapters::tmux::tests::shell_session_with_env_cwd_and_scrollback
each binary, serially:
 40.07 s  dispatch/first_slice
  5.54 s  dispatch/dispatch (lib)
  5.44 s  gate
  3.48 s  switchboard (lib)
  1.11 s  ui
  0.28 s  control
 55.92 s  in all
```

`cargo test --locked --workspace` took 37 s of wall time in parallel on
the same machine, built. The two gate tests at the top spend most of
their time holding still on purpose (half-second and two-second windows
in which nothing may happen). Measure on a quiet machine: another
checkout running its tests at the same time makes every file operation
wait behind its device flushes, and the same script then reads ten
times slower.

Requirements: macOS, `tmux` 3.2 or newer (`brew install tmux`), Ghostty
for agent sessions, `cmake` (`brew install cmake`; the embedded Prompt Box
builds whisper.cpp), and `claude` and/or `codex` on `PATH`. The app tells
you at the bottom of the window when tmux is missing. Prompt Box is a git
dependency pinned by revision; if cargo cannot fetch it because a git
`insteadOf` rule turns the URL into ssh, run with
`CARGO_NET_GIT_FETCH_WITH_CLI=true` (or set `net.git-fetch-with-cli` in
`~/.cargo/config.toml`) so the git CLI's credentials are used. The
bundle declares microphone use (`NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`): a
bundled app without it gets silence from the microphone, no prompt and
no error, so listening looks dead.

Data lives in `~/Library/Application Support/Switchboard/`: one JSON file
per project under `projects/` (with a `.bak` of the previous version;
approvals of defined commands live inside these records),
`launch.log` (what the last launch loaded and chose for the main
window's frame, for a launch with no terminal to log to),
`operations.log` and `control.sock` (the control port: every command
another process sent, its reply, and the socket it came in on; see
`docs/dispatch.md`),
`identity.json` (the remote port's identity: the server id, its display
name, the self-signed certificate and its key hash, and whether the
port listens on the local network and on which port; the certificate's
private key is in the Keychain) and `devices.json` (the devices paired
with this host: name, scope, when paired and last seen, and the SHA-256
of each bearer token, never the token; see `docs/remote-client.md`),
`settings.json` (theme, the active workspace, editor, global variables, file
side shown next to sessions and its tab, the directory each project's
file side starts at when narrowed, the screen to reopen on, the
Prompt Box switch and its trigger word, model, captions, and the screen
its caption bar and preview panel appear on, the sessions open in
windows of their own and where each window sits, where the main
window sits, the zoom of each display, the workflow round cap and the
user's workflow definitions, and the environment sets: each set's
variables, which of them are secret, and its AWS method),
`views.json` (schema v7: the workspaces, and the working sets: each
one's name, workspace, which sessions and files are on it, and where
each card sits on its grid, with a `.bak`; a set made in the global
workspace, "Everywhere", is in no real workspace and may hold cards
from all of them; a rule set stores its rule, such as "active in the
last 24 hours", the sessions dismissed from it, whether it shows
only running sessions, and its card size instead of cards),
the
`tmux.conf`, `claude-hooks.json` (passed to Claude Code
with `--settings`), `events.log` (the hook event log; a
`UserPromptSubmit` line carries `injected`, never the prompt; a `Stop`
line carries `tasks` and `crons`, kinds and schedules only),
`crons/` (one file per Claude Code session: a hash of each cron prompt
the last `Stop` listed, never the text; removed when the session starts
or ends, and swept after a day),
`wake.sock`, and
`scrollback/` (one `<host>-r<n>.vt` per run of a command or service,
the last 20 runs kept), `renders/` (first pages of PDFs shown on cards,
rasterized by Quick Look), and `workflows/<run>/round-<n>/` (copies of
the plan, feedback, and response at the end of each review round). Sessions run
on a private tmux server (`tmux -L switchboard`), never on your default
one. Nothing is written into a project directory except what the Config
editor saves on your click. Secret values live in the login Keychain,
never in these files, under the accounts `global/<VAR>`,
`project/<id>/<VAR>` and `set/<name>/<VAR>` (an environment set's), and
`remote-key:<server id>` (the remote port's private key, as PEM).

### Defining commands and services

A project can declare its commands and services in
`<root>/.switchboard/project.json`, so an agent working in the project
can set them up for you:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "commands": [
    { "name": "rebundle", "command": "./scripts/bundle.sh" },
    { "name": "lint", "command": "cargo clippy", "cwd": "crates/app", "env": ["RUSTFLAGS"] },
    { "name": "report", "command": "make report", "output": ["out/report.pdf", "out/*.md"] }
  ],
  "services": [
    { "name": "web", "command": "npm run dev", "autostart": true }
  ],
  "show": ["manager", "orchard-backend"]
}
```

`show` lists folders under the root that the file side lists even when
the root's `.gitignore` hides them, such as sub-repositories checked out
inside a workspace directory. Each is walked as its own tree: its own
`.gitignore` applies, the root's does not. Entries must be relative
paths without `..`; others are skipped with a warning.

Names are 1 to 64 characters and unique across both lists; `cwd` is
relative to the project root and may not use `..`; `env` lists the
variable names the command expects (values come from the project's
environment, never from this file); `output` is a glob pattern or a
list of them, relative to the command's directory, naming the files a
run produces: those written during the run are listed on the command's
card and page afterwards, with a Markdown or PDF file shown in place.
An entry with an unknown field or
a bad value is skipped with a warning that names it; the rest still
load. The file is limited to 64 KiB and must not be a symlink.

Nothing in the file runs until you approve the entry in the Run tab,
where you see the command, its directory, and the variables it asks
for. Any change to an entry drops its approval; `autostart` is honored
only for approved services. The board's Config button opens the file
for editing, with the options listed beside it and the parse result shown
as you type; Save is the only time Switchboard writes into
`.switchboard/`.

## App bundle

```sh
./scripts/bundle.sh          # installs ~/Applications/Switchboard.app
./scripts/bump.sh minor      # the next version into Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and CHANGELOG.md
./scripts/release.sh         # publishes the committed version as a GitHub release (--dry-run: build and zip only)
./scripts/icon.sh            # regenerates the icons from assets/Switchboard.svg and assets/vision/*.svg
```

The bundle carries the binaries side by side in `Contents/MacOS`:
`switchboard`, `switchboard-hook` (which the app locates next to its own
executable), `switchboard-env` and `switchboard-ask` (which Dispatch
locates next to its own) and `dispatch`. Raising a Ghostty
window needs Accessibility, and macOS ties that grant to the code
signature, and the Keychain ties its per-item "always allow" to the
signer's Team ID. The script signs with `CODESIGN_IDENTITY`, else the
first "Developer ID Application" identity (has a Team ID, so Keychain
items stay allowed across rebuilds), else a "Switchboard Dev" or "Prompt
Box Dev" certificate from Keychain Access (keeps the Accessibility grant,
but the Keychain asks for its items again after each build), else ad-hoc
(the grant is reset each rebuild). `scripts/icon.sh`
renders the SVG with AppKit into `assets/Switchboard.icns` for Finder and
`assets/icon-256.rgba`, which `src/main.rs` embeds for the Dock, and the
three layers of the visionOS icon (`assets/vision/*.svg`, the same
drawing split for the headset's parallax and circular mask) into the
client's asset catalog.

Releases are numbered by [semantic versioning](https://semver.org) and
listed in `CHANGELOG.md`; the version in `Cargo.toml` is the one source,
and it reaches the binary (`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, shown at the
bottom of the Settings menu), the bundle's `Info.plist` and the host's
`/info` reply (the headset shows it beside each host). A release is
three steps:

```sh
./scripts/bump.sh minor          # or patch, major, or X.Y.Z: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, CHANGELOG.md
git commit -am "Release 0.3.0"   # after a look at the diff
./scripts/release.sh             # builds, signs, zips, tags v0.3.0, publishes with the changelog section
```

Every user-visible change adds a line under Unreleased in
`CHANGELOG.md` as it lands, so the bump has something to move.
`scripts/release.sh` builds the bundle through `bundle.sh` into a
staging directory, zips it with `ditto` (a plain `zip` would lose the
signature), writes the zip's SHA-256 as a file of its own, tags the
commit `v<version>` and attaches both to a GitHub release whose notes
are the changelog's section. It refuses a dirty tree, a version without
a changelog section, and a tag that exists.

A running Switchboard checks the repository's latest release twenty
seconds after launch and hourly (`core::updates`, the
`adapters::updates::GitHubReleases` source over `ureq`). A newer version
is a notice and an "Update" item on the rail: the click downloads the
zip to `$TMPDIR/switchboard-update`, checks it against the published
SHA-256, unpacks it with `ditto`, verifies the bundle's signature with
`codesign` and requires its Team ID to equal the running app's (so the
Accessibility and Keychain grants keyed on the signature survive), and
then offers "Restart to update": a helper script waits for the process
to exit, moves the old bundle to `.Switchboard.app.previous` beside it,
copies the new one in and relaunches it, putting the old one back if the
copy fails (its output is in `$TMPDIR/switchboard-update/swap.log`). A
bare `cargo run` binary, an unsigned bundle or one outside a writable
directory refuses to install and says so. A pre-release tag or one that
does not parse is never offered.

Another Mac installs a release by hand, with `tmux`, Ghostty and `gh`
installed:

```sh
gh release download v0.2.0 -R msull/switchboard -p 'Switchboard-*.zip' -D ~/Downloads
ditto -x -k ~/Downloads/Switchboard-0.2.0.zip ~/Applications
open ~/Applications/Switchboard.app
```

`gh` and `curl` set no quarantine flag, so Gatekeeper asks nothing of
the bundle, which is signed but not notarized; a browser download
carries the flag, and `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <app>` clears
it. From then on the app updates itself. That Mac makes its own
identity and key on first launch, so it is a second host to the remote
client, never a copy of this one.

Dev aids, all environment variables:

- `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR=<dir>`: use another data directory (keep the path
  short; the wake socket path has a 104-byte limit). The app sets it in
  every pane it spawns, so `switchboard-env` in a shell asks the
  instance that launched it.
- `SWITCHBOARD_RECORD_TOKEN`: set by the app in every pane, beside
  `SWITCHBOARD_RECORD_ID`, and new at every spawn. `switchboard-env
  exec` sends it with `env.resolve`; the record keeps only its SHA-256.
  To try `switchboard-env` by hand, run it in a shell the app launched,
  after `env-setup unlock` (or the settings menu's Unlock environment
  setup) for the setup commands. `switchboard-ask` sends it too, with
  `session.ask`; `switchboard-ask "a question"` in a shell the app
  launched marks that shell's card as waiting on you, and
  `switchboard-ask --clear` takes the mark off. A Claude Code session
  may add `--confirm`, `--choice "<option>"` (once per option) or
  `--text`; the owner answers on the card, and the answer comes back
  as the session's next prompt, `Owner answered "<question>": <answer>`,
  once its turn has ended.
- `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET=<name>`: use another tmux socket name.
- `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT=<port>`: bind the remote port there instead
  of the port in `identity.json`, so two instances can run on one
  machine; `0` picks a free one. The port answers `/api/v1/info` to
  anyone and every other read to a paired device; pair one from the
  settings menu's Remote devices dialog, and read with the token it
  was given (`curl --insecure` trusts any certificate; a real client
  pins the key hash the dialog shows):
  `curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://127.0.0.1:43187/api/v1/waiting`.
  The Swift client's command-line browser does the pinned version:
  `client/README.md`; the dialog's "Copy invite" puts the QR code's
  text on the clipboard, so `switchboard-remote pair "$(pbpaste)"`
  pairs it. Script lines `remote-listen lan <port>` and
  `pairing <code>` put an instance on the network with a window open.
- `DISPATCH_DATA_DIR=<dir>`: where the Dispatch page looks for
  `dispatch.sock` and where its console opens (the `dispatch` binary
  reads the same variable). Tickets' trees go under
  `~/.dispatch/worktrees` regardless, or wherever `dispatch worktrees
  <path>` (also on the Dispatch page) points; the setting is
  `<dir>/settings.json`. `<dir>/events.jsonl` is the event log
  `dispatch events` and `wait` read, and `<dir>/runner.json` the
  runner's status after its last pass, which `dispatch health` reads.
  `<dir>/lock` is the writer lock, with a line naming its holder, and
  `<dir>/tickets/<id>/closing.lock` is held by whichever `dispatch` is
  finishing that ticket's close; both are lock files, not records.
  `<dir>/tickets/<id>/<stage>/<n>/<context>/<name>/` (mode 0700) holds a
  stage's evidence files. It is removed `evidence_keep_days` after the
  ticket closes, or at close with `--drop-evidence`.
  `<dir>/tickets/<id>/usage.json` caches the token counts, model names
  and timestamps read from the ticket's sessions' transcripts, never
  their content, so `report` and the Usage tab keep them after Claude
  Code deletes the transcripts.
  `<dir>/projects/<project>/supervisor/` holds a project's supervisor
  files: `seed.md`, the prompt its session starts from, `handoff.md`,
  which the session keeps, and `handoff.<stamp>.md`, each earlier
  hand-off kept when a fresh session replaced it. The supervisor works
  in `supervisor-<project>` under the worktrees root. The project's
  record `<dir>/projects/<project>.json` keeps the supervisor's sessions
  and, in `supervision.refusals`, the last 20 commands it was refused
  for want of a `may` capability.
  The overview's Start runs `dispatch run` as the app's `runner`
  service in that directory, and the runner reaches this app through its
  own `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR`, so a dev instance should point
  `DISPATCH_DATA_DIR` at a throwaway directory before Start. A `cargo
  run` finds a runner to start only once `cargo build -p dispatch` has
  put `dispatch` beside the app binary; otherwise Start is refused.
- `SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT=<file>`: run actions at startup, one per line, so
  the app can be put into a known state without clicking. See
  `src/script.rs` for the lines (`add-project`, `new-shell`, `new-claude`,
  `new-codex`, `new-service`, `show-board`, `show-session`, `show-document`,
  `show-file`, `files`, `side-position`, `terminal`, `select-file`,
  `set-env`, `set-secret`, `dotenv`, `environment`, `config`,
  `env-setup unlock|lock`, `pairing <code>|close`, `remote-devices`,
  `remote-listen lan|loopback <port>`,
  `send`, `interrupt`, `return`, `kill`, `remove`, `approve`, `revoke`, `side`,
  `switchboard`, `working-set`, `new-working-set`, `clone-working-set`,
  `rename-working-set`, `delete-working-set`, `new-recent-set`,
  `set-hours`, `running-only`, `card-scale`, `dismiss-from-set`, `add-to-working-set`,
  `add-file-to-working-set`, `arrange`, `show-message`, `clone-session`,
  `discard-to`, `undo-discard`, `review-plan`, `show-review`,
  `show-dispatch`, `dispatch-runner-start`, `dispatch-runner-stop`,
  `show-ticket`, `close-ticket`, `ticket-tab` (`<id>` and one of
  `timeline`, `issue`, `plan`, `notes`, `review`, `changes`, `usage`), `ticket-diff`,
  `review-file`, `review-continue`, `review-object`, `review-finalize`, `show-artifact`,
  `pop-out`, `close-pop-out`, `files-root`, `zoom`, `place-pop-out`,
  `place-card`, `new-workspace`, `workspace`, `workspace-global`,
  `move-project`, `move-working-set`, `controller`,
  `open-terminal`, `prompt-box`, `theme`, `sleep`).
- `SWITCHBOARD_CONTROLLER=<device>`: the nunchuk's serial port (default: the
  `/dev/cu.usbmodem*` whose USB product name is Feather or MagTag, waited
  for if absent; no other board is ever opened, since a port that never answers
  blocks the process in the kernel at exit).
- `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX=<path>`: tmux binary to use.
- `RUST_LOG=switchboard=debug`: verbose logging.

Live tests that spend money or open windows are `#[ignore]`d:

```sh
cargo test --test live -- --ignored --nocapture     # one cheap claude, codex, and Ghostty run each
cargo test --test gate -- --ignored --nocapture     # the Milestone 1 gate items that need real agents
```

### Layout

```
src/main.rs              launcher: wires real adapters, opens the window
src/bin/switchboard-hook.rs  helper Claude Code hooks call (std only)
src/bin/switchboard-env.rs   runs one child with a session's environment sets, resolved over the control port with its launch token; the sets' setup commands (std and the wire crate only)
src/bin/switchboard-ask.rs   marks the session it runs in as asking the owner a one-line question, or a confirm, a choice or a line of text whose answer comes back as its next prompt, or clears it, over the control port with its launch token (std and the wire crate only)
src/lib.rs               module tree and the layering rules
src/core/
  model.rs               durable data model (Project, SessionRecord, ResumeHandle, CardState)
  action.rs              AppAction, Effect, Clock, AppCore::dispatch, read model for the UI
  reconcile.rs           StoreLoaded / HostListed: card states, autostart services, spawn specs
  sessions.rs            launch, idempotent return, resume preflight, Codex serialization
  grid.rs                Working Set placement: default card sizes, first free spot, overlap, minimum size, the card a step away, a rule set's card size at its scale and flowed layout
  controller.rs          the hand controller's meaning: the selected card per working set, Z's radial menu, the session C holds open
  definitions.rs         .switchboard/project.json entries -> records; hash-keyed approval
  env.rs                 environment resolution for a new session: global variables, opted-in .env files, the project's own; secrets by account name
  file_refs.rs           file paths in an agent's prose as links: finder, rewrite given which name a file, per-message cache
  events.rs              hook events -> record activity (matched by record id, ordered by time)
  workflow.rs            plan review runs: reviewer and planner rounds as a state machine over records
  control.rs             the control port's commands run quietly under an operation id; read models in the wire's shapes; `ready_for_prompt`, the one verdict `session.prompt` and a view's `prompt_refusal` share
  remote.rs              the remote port's state: the host's identity and paired devices as loaded, the pairing window with its code, scope and failure count, a device's scope and revocation
  updates.rs             the app's version and its update: the scheduled check, a newer release offered, downloaded on a click and installed on another; semantic versions, pre-releases never offered
  tickets.rs             Dispatch's tickets as the remote port says them: each ticket's summary with its standing worded as the Mac's page words it, its decisions, and alone its body, attempts and lanes; one value for the port's fingerprint and its replies
  revision.rs            the read-model fingerprints behind the remote port's revision: every exported view hashed with its time-derived fields held still, and the `changed`/`removed` diff between two passes (and a record's runs as the `runs` collection)
  diff.rs                a changed file's diff as held per ticket, lane and path, when a re-read is due, which unchanged runs fold

The flow for any feature: the UI dispatches an `AppAction`; the core
updates its state and returns `Effect`s; the app runs each effect through
an adapter and dispatches the result as another action. Add a capability by
adding a port trait, a real adapter, a fake, and an `Effect` variant. The
core never touches egui, threads, files, or the network.

### Testing approach

Everything enters `AppCore::dispatch(action, clock)` and leaves as effects,
so core tests are plain state-transition tests with an explicit clock and
no sleeping. Adapters get their own tests where they have logic. UI tests
run the real `eframe::App` headlessly with fake adapters, find widgets by
label, and advance frames with `harness.run_steps(2)`: one frame to
process the click, one to render its result.

A test that waits on a real process (a tmux pane, a child process, a
thread's result) polls to a deadline through its file's helper
(`poll_on` in the tmux adapter, `poll_to`, `wait_until` and `hold` in
`tests/gate.rs`, `frames_until` in `tests/ui.rs`, `poll_to` in
Dispatch's `git.rs`) and never sleeps a fixed time before an assert.
Dispatch's integration tests skip the device flush
(`store::skip_fsync_for_tests`) and move time with `Env::wait` rather
than stepping through it.

Tests that hit real services (a model, a paid API) go in their own
`tests/*.rs` file, marked `#[ignore]`, with the command to run them
documented here.

### Pre-commit hook

`.githooks/pre-commit` checks formatting, runs Clippy, and runs the tests
before each commit, including the vendored terminal widget's tests, which
`--workspace` does not reach because `vendor/egui_term` is excluded. It
never modifies or stages files. Enable it once per clone:

```sh
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

### Secrets

Local secrets go in `.env` (ignored by git). Read them from the app at
startup; never bake them into the binary or commit them.

# Switchboard

A desktop app for organizing, managing, and automating agent coding
sessions. Built in Rust with [egui](https://docs.rs/egui) /
[eframe](https://docs.rs/eframe) from
[egui-app-template](../egui-app-template); design notes live in `docs/`.

Requires Rust 1.95 or newer.

## Development

```sh
cargo run --locked                                   # launch the app
cargo test --locked --workspace                      # unit + headless UI + tmux integration tests, every crate
cargo test --locked -p egui_term --lib               # the vendored terminal widget (outside the workspace)
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   # lint
cargo fmt --all                                      # format
(cd client && swift test)                            # the Swift client's packages, 81 tests (Xcode; not in the hook or CI)
(cd client && scripts/sim.sh run)                    # the visionOS app on the simulator (xcodegen; see client/README.md)
./scripts/test-times.sh                              # every test timed serially, the slowest ten, the budget checked
```

under two minutes locally; `scripts/test-times.sh` checks the first and

Requirements: macOS, `tmux` 3.2 or newer (`brew install tmux`), Ghostty
for agent sessions, `cmake` (`brew install cmake`; the embedded Prompt Box
builds whisper.cpp), and `claude` and/or `codex` on `PATH`. The app tells
you at the bottom of the window when tmux is missing. Prompt Box is a git
dependency pinned by revision; if cargo cannot fetch it because a git
`insteadOf` rule turns the URL into ssh, run with
`CARGO_NET_GIT_FETCH_WITH_CLI=true` (or set `net.git-fetch-with-cli` in
`~/.cargo/config.toml`) so the git CLI's credentials are used. The
bundle declares microphone use (`NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`): a
bundled app without it gets silence from the microphone, no prompt and
no error, so listening looks dead.

Data lives in `~/Library/Application Support/Switchboard/`: one JSON file
per project under `projects/` (with a `.bak` of the previous version;
approvals of defined commands live inside these records),
`launch.log` (what the last launch loaded and chose for the main
window's frame, for a launch with no terminal to log to),
`operations.log` and `control.sock` (the control port: every command
another process sent, its reply, and the socket it came in on; see
`docs/dispatch.md`),
`identity.json` (the remote port's identity: the server id, its display
name, the self-signed certificate and its key hash, and whether the
port listens on the local network and on which port; the certificate's
private key is in the Keychain) and `devices.json` (the devices paired
with this host: name, scope, when paired and last seen, and the SHA-256
of each bearer token, never the token; see `docs/remote-client.md`),
`settings.json` (theme, the active workspace, editor, global variables, file
side shown next to sessions and its tab, the directory each project's
file side starts at when narrowed, the screen to reopen on, the
Prompt Box switch and its trigger word, model, captions, and the screen
its caption bar and preview panel appear on, the sessions open in
windows of their own and where each window sits, where the main
window sits, the zoom of each display, the workflow round cap and the
user's workflow definitions, and the environment sets: each set's
variables, which of them are secret, and its AWS method),
`views.json` (schema v7: the workspaces, and the working sets: each
one's name, workspace, which sessions and files are on it, and where
each card sits on its grid, with a `.bak`; a set made in the global
workspace, "Everywhere", is in no real workspace and may hold cards
from all of them; a rule set stores its rule, such as "active in the
last 24 hours", the sessions dismissed from it, whether it shows
only running sessions, and its card size instead of cards),
the
`tmux.conf`, `claude-hooks.json` (passed to Claude Code
with `--settings`), `events.log` (the hook event log; a
`UserPromptSubmit` line carries `injected`, never the prompt; a `Stop`
line carries `tasks` and `crons`, kinds and schedules only),
`crons/` (one file per Claude Code session: a hash of each cron prompt
the last `Stop` listed, never the text; removed when the session starts
or ends, and swept after a day),
`wake.sock`, and
`scrollback/` (one `<host>-r<n>.vt` per run of a command or service,
the last 20 runs kept), `renders/` (first pages of PDFs shown on cards,
rasterized by Quick Look), and `workflows/<run>/round-<n>/` (copies of
the plan, feedback, and response at the end of each review round). Sessions run
on a private tmux server (`tmux -L switchboard`), never on your default
one. Nothing is written into a project directory except what the Config
editor saves on your click. Secret values live in the login Keychain,
never in these files, under the accounts `global/<VAR>`,
`project/<id>/<VAR>` and `set/<name>/<VAR>` (an environment set's), and
`remote-key:<server id>` (the remote port's private key, as PEM).

### Defining commands and services

A project can declare its commands and services in
`<root>/.switchboard/project.json`, so an agent working in the project
can set them up for you:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "commands": [
    { "name": "rebundle", "command": "./scripts/bundle.sh" },
    { "name": "lint", "command": "cargo clippy", "cwd": "crates/app", "env": ["RUSTFLAGS"] },
    { "name": "report", "command": "make report", "output": ["out/report.pdf", "out/*.md"] }
  ],
  "services": [
    { "name": "web", "command": "npm run dev", "autostart": true }
  ],
  "show": ["manager", "orchard-backend"]
}
```

`show` lists folders under the root that the file side lists even when
the root's `.gitignore` hides them, such as sub-repositories checked out
inside a workspace directory. Each is walked as its own tree: its own
`.gitignore` applies, the root's does not. Entries must be relative
paths without `..`; others are skipped with a warning.

Names are 1 to 64 characters and unique across both lists; `cwd` is
relative to the project root and may not use `..`; `env` lists the
variable names the command expects (values come from the project's
environment, never from this file); `output` is a glob pattern or a
list of them, relative to the command's directory, naming the files a
run produces: those written during the run are listed on the command's
card and page afterwards, with a Markdown or PDF file shown in place.
An entry with an unknown field or
a bad value is skipped with a warning that names it; the rest still
load. The file is limited to 64 KiB and must not be a symlink.

Nothing in the file runs until you approve the entry in the Run tab,
where you see the command, its directory, and the variables it asks
for. Any change to an entry drops its approval; `autostart` is honored
only for approved services. The board's Config button opens the file
for editing, with the options listed beside it and the parse result shown
as you type; Save is the only time Switchboard writes into
`.switchboard/`.

## App bundle

```sh
./scripts/bundle.sh          # installs ~/Applications/Switchboard.app
./scripts/bump.sh minor      # the next version into Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and CHANGELOG.md
./scripts/release.sh         # publishes the committed version as a GitHub release (--dry-run: build and zip only)
./scripts/icon.sh            # regenerates the icons from assets/Switchboard.svg and assets/vision/*.svg
```

The bundle carries the binaries side by side in `Contents/MacOS`:
`switchboard`, `switchboard-hook` (which the app locates next to its own
executable), `switchboard-env` and `switchboard-ask` (which Dispatch
locates next to its own) and `dispatch`. Raising a Ghostty
window needs Accessibility, and macOS ties that grant to the code
signature, and the Keychain ties its per-item "always allow" to the
signer's Team ID. The script signs with `CODESIGN_IDENTITY`, else the
first "Developer ID Application" identity (has a Team ID, so Keychain
items stay allowed across rebuilds), else a "Switchboard Dev" or "Prompt
Box Dev" certificate from Keychain Access (keeps the Accessibility grant,
but the Keychain asks for its items again after each build), else ad-hoc
(the grant is reset each rebuild). `scripts/icon.sh`
renders the SVG with AppKit into `assets/Switchboard.icns` for Finder and
`assets/icon-256.rgba`, which `src/main.rs` embeds for the Dock, and the
three layers of the visionOS icon (`assets/vision/*.svg`, the same
drawing split for the headset's parallax and circular mask) into the
client's asset catalog.

Releases are numbered by [semantic versioning](https://semver.org) and
listed in `CHANGELOG.md`; the version in `Cargo.toml` is the one source,
and it reaches the binary (`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, shown at the
bottom of the Settings menu), the bundle's `Info.plist` and the host's
`/info` reply (the headset shows it beside each host). A release is
three steps:

```sh
./scripts/bump.sh minor          # or patch, major, or X.Y.Z: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, CHANGELOG.md
git commit -am "Release 0.3.0"   # after a look at the diff
./scripts/release.sh             # builds, signs, zips, tags v0.3.0, publishes with the changelog section
```

Every user-visible change adds a line under Unreleased in
`CHANGELOG.md` as it lands, so the bump has something to move.
`scripts/release.sh` builds the bundle through `bundle.sh` into a
staging directory, zips it with `ditto` (a plain `zip` would lose the
signature), writes the zip's SHA-256 as a file of its own, tags the
commit `v<version>` and attaches both to a GitHub release whose notes
are the changelog's section. It refuses a dirty tree, a version without
a changelog section, and a tag that exists.

A running Switchboard checks the repository's latest release twenty
seconds after launch and hourly (`core::updates`, the
`adapters::updates::GitHubReleases` source over `ureq`). A newer version
is a notice and an "Update" item on the rail: the click downloads the
zip to `$TMPDIR/switchboard-update`, checks it against the published
SHA-256, unpacks it with `ditto`, verifies the bundle's signature with
`codesign` and requires its Team ID to equal the running app's (so the
Accessibility and Keychain grants keyed on the signature survive), and
then offers "Restart to update": a helper script waits for the process
to exit, moves the old bundle to `.Switchboard.app.previous` beside it,
copies the new one in and relaunches it, putting the old one back if the
copy fails (its output is in `$TMPDIR/switchboard-update/swap.log`). A
bare `cargo run` binary, an unsigned bundle or one outside a writable
directory refuses to install and says so. A pre-release tag or one that
does not parse is never offered.

Another Mac installs a release by hand, with `tmux`, Ghostty and `gh`
installed:

```sh
gh release download v0.2.0 -R msull/switchboard -p 'Switchboard-*.zip' -D ~/Downloads
ditto -x -k ~/Downloads/Switchboard-0.2.0.zip ~/Applications
open ~/Applications/Switchboard.app
```

`gh` and `curl` set no quarantine flag, so Gatekeeper asks nothing of
the bundle, which is signed but not notarized; a browser download
carries the flag, and `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <app>` clears
it. From then on the app updates itself. That Mac makes its own
identity and key on first launch, so it is a second host to the remote
client, never a copy of this one.

Dev aids, all environment variables:

- `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR=<dir>`: use another data directory (keep the path
  short; the wake socket path has a 104-byte limit). The app sets it in
  every pane it spawns, so `switchboard-env` in a shell asks the
  instance that launched it.
- `SWITCHBOARD_RECORD_TOKEN`: set by the app in every pane, beside
  `SWITCHBOARD_RECORD_ID`, and new at every spawn. `switchboard-env
  exec` sends it with `env.resolve`; the record keeps only its SHA-256.
  To try `switchboard-env` by hand, run it in a shell the app launched,
  after `env-setup unlock` (or the settings menu's Unlock environment
  setup) for the setup commands. `switchboard-ask` sends it too, with
  `session.ask`; `switchboard-ask "a question"` in a shell the app
  launched marks that shell's card as waiting on you, and
  `switchboard-ask --clear` takes the mark off. A Claude Code session
  may add `--confirm`, `--choice "<option>"` (once per option) or
  `--text`; the owner answers on the card, and the answer comes back
  as the session's next prompt, `Owner answered "<question>": <answer>`,
  once its turn has ended.
- `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET=<name>`: use another tmux socket name.
- `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT=<port>`: bind the remote port there instead
  of the port in `identity.json`, so two instances can run on one
  machine; `0` picks a free one. The port answers `/api/v1/info` to
  anyone and every other read to a paired device; pair one from the
  settings menu's Remote devices dialog, and read with the token it
  was given (`curl --insecure` trusts any certificate; a real client
  pins the key hash the dialog shows):
  `curl -sk -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://127.0.0.1:43187/api/v1/waiting`.
  The Swift client's command-line browser does the pinned version:
  `client/README.md`; the dialog's "Copy invite" puts the QR code's
  text on the clipboard, so `switchboard-remote pair "$(pbpaste)"`
  pairs it. Script lines `remote-listen lan <port>` and
  `pairing <code>` put an instance on the network with a window open.
- `DISPATCH_DATA_DIR=<dir>`: where the Dispatch page looks for
  `dispatch.sock` and where its console opens (the `dispatch` binary
  reads the same variable). Tickets' trees go under
  `~/.dispatch/worktrees` regardless, or wherever `dispatch worktrees
  <path>` (also on the Dispatch page) points; the setting is
  `<dir>/settings.json`. `<dir>/events.jsonl` is the event log
  `dispatch events` and `wait` read, and `<dir>/runner.json` the
  runner's status after its last pass, which `dispatch health` reads.
  `<dir>/lock` is the writer lock, with a line naming its holder, and
  `<dir>/tickets/<id>/closing.lock` is held by whichever `dispatch` is
  finishing that ticket's close; both are lock files, not records.
  `<dir>/tickets/<id>/<stage>/<n>/<context>/<name>/` (mode 0700) holds a
  stage's evidence files. It is removed `evidence_keep_days` after the
  ticket closes, or at close with `--drop-evidence`.
  `<dir>/tickets/<id>/usage.json` caches the token counts, model names
  and timestamps read from the ticket's sessions' transcripts, never
  their content, so `report` and the Usage tab keep them after Claude
  Code deletes the transcripts.
  `<dir>/projects/<project>/supervisor/` holds a project's supervisor
  files: `seed.md`, the prompt its session starts from, `handoff.md`,
  which the session keeps, and `handoff.<stamp>.md`, each earlier
  hand-off kept when a fresh session replaced it. The supervisor works
  in `supervisor-<project>` under the worktrees root. The project's
  record `<dir>/projects/<project>.json` keeps the supervisor's sessions
  and, in `supervision.refusals`, the last 20 commands it was refused
  for want of a `may` capability.
  The overview's Start runs `dispatch run` as the app's `runner`
  service in that directory, and the runner reaches this app through its
  own `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR`, so a dev instance should point
  `DISPATCH_DATA_DIR` at a throwaway directory before Start. A `cargo
  run` finds a runner to start only once `cargo build -p dispatch` has
  put `dispatch` beside the app binary; otherwise Start is refused.
- `SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT=<file>`: run actions at startup, one per line, so
  the app can be put into a known state without clicking. See
  `src/script.rs` for the lines (`add-project`, `new-shell`, `new-claude`,
  `new-codex`, `new-service`, `show-board`, `show-session`, `show-document`,
  `show-file`, `files`, `side-position`, `terminal`, `select-file`,
  `set-env`, `set-secret`, `dotenv`, `environment`, `config`,
  `env-setup unlock|lock`, `pairing <code>|close`, `remote-devices`,
  `remote-listen lan|loopback <port>`,
  `send`, `interrupt`, `return`, `kill`, `remove`, `approve`, `revoke`, `side`,
  `switchboard`, `working-set`, `new-working-set`, `clone-working-set`,
  `rename-working-set`, `delete-working-set`, `new-recent-set`,
  `set-hours`, `running-only`, `card-scale`, `dismiss-from-set`, `add-to-working-set`,
  `add-file-to-working-set`, `arrange`, `show-message`, `clone-session`,
  `discard-to`, `undo-discard`, `review-plan`, `show-review`,
  `show-dispatch`, `dispatch-runner-start`, `dispatch-runner-stop`,
  `show-ticket`, `close-ticket`, `ticket-tab` (`<id>` and one of
  `timeline`, `issue`, `plan`, `notes`, `review`, `changes`, `usage`), `ticket-diff`,
  `review-file`, `review-continue`, `review-object`, `review-finalize`, `show-artifact`,
  `pop-out`, `close-pop-out`, `files-root`, `zoom`, `place-pop-out`,
  `place-card`, `new-workspace`, `workspace`, `workspace-global`,
  `move-project`, `move-working-set`, `controller`,
  `open-terminal`, `prompt-box`, `theme`, `sleep`).
- `SWITCHBOARD_CONTROLLER=<device>`: the nunchuk's serial port (default: the
  `/dev/cu.usbmodem*` whose USB product name is Feather or MagTag, waited
  for if absent; no other board is ever opened, since a port that never answers
  blocks the process in the kernel at exit).
- `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX=<path>`: tmux binary to use.
- `RUST_LOG=switchboard=debug`: verbose logging.

Live tests that spend money or open windows are `#[ignore]`d:

```sh
cargo test --test live -- --ignored --nocapture     # one cheap claude, codex, and Ghostty run each
cargo test --test gate -- --ignored --nocapture     # the Milestone 1 gate items that need real agents
```

The flow for any feature: the UI dispatches an `AppAction`; the core
updates its state and returns `Effect`s; the app runs each effect through
an adapter and dispatches the result as another action. Add a capability by
adding a port trait, a real adapter, a fake, and an `Effect` variant. The
core never touches egui, threads, files, or the network.

### Testing approach

Everything enters `AppCore::dispatch(action, clock)` and leaves as effects,
so core tests are plain state-transition tests with an explicit clock and
no sleeping. Adapters get their own tests where they have logic. UI tests
run the real `eframe::App` headlessly with fake adapters, find widgets by
label, and advance frames with `harness.run_steps(2)`: one frame to
process the click, one to render its result.

A test that waits on a real process (a tmux pane, a child process, a
thread's result) polls to a deadline through its file's helper
(`poll_on` in the tmux adapter, `poll_to`, `wait_until` and `hold` in
`tests/gate.rs`, `frames_until` in `tests/ui.rs`, `poll_to` in
Dispatch's `git.rs`) and never sleeps a fixed time before an assert.
Dispatch's integration tests skip the device flush
(`store::skip_fsync_for_tests`) and move time with `Env::wait` rather
than stepping through it.

Tests that hit real services (a model, a paid API) go in their own
`tests/*.rs` file, marked `#[ignore]`, with the command to run them
documented here.

### Pre-commit hook

`.githooks/pre-commit` checks formatting, runs Clippy, and runs the tests
before each commit, including the vendored terminal widget's tests, which
`--workspace` does not reach because `vendor/egui_term` is excluded. It
never modifies or stages files. Enable it once per clone:

```sh
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

### Secrets

Local secrets go in `.env` (ignored by git). Read them from the app at
startup; never bake them into the binary or commit them.
